summary.summary: Calderdale ended 2025/26 with just £2.68m of external investments — a single NatWest call account, down from £6.2m a year earlier — against £137.6m of PWLB debt: the cash cushion is essentially gone. The report is unusually candid about why: years of SEND (schools funding) deficits and reserve drawdowns have worsened cashflow, forcing rolling short-term borrowing from other councils (£305k of interest in the year) even as £9.98m of PWLB debt matured without replacement. Treasury costs overran budget by £654k because investment income fell £1.54m short of plan. Internal borrowing will need replacing with new long-term PWLB loans in 2026/27, so a step-up in external debt is coming against a CFR of £237.3m.

signals.headline: External investments of £2.68m at 31 March 2026 (one NatWest call account; £6.2m a year earlier) against £137.6m of PWLB debt
signals.why: With almost no invested cash, day-to-day spending depends on continuously rolling short-term loans from other councils.

signals.headline: The SEND funding deficit 'accumulated over a number of years continued to significantly impact on the Council's cashflow throughout' 2025/26, driving increased short-term borrowing
signals.why: A schools deficit parked behind the statutory accounting override is being financed with real borrowed cash today.

signals.headline: 'Significant levels of Council reserves have been used' in recent years to fund additional costs and the increased SEND deficit, reducing balances and forcing short-term borrowing
signals.why: The cash that once backed reserves is spent, so internal borrowing capacity is exhausted and new pressure lands directly on external debt.

findings.paper_title: Item 8 First Quart Financial Outturn Position - Revenue and Capital Monitor Q1FINAL
findings.headline: Capital programme £371.8m funded 40% from borrowing (£151.4m) across 2026/27-2029/30 period
findings.detail: Revised capital programme totals £371.8m, with financing split 52% external grants (£195.9m), 40% borrowing (£151.4m), and remainder from revenue and pooled resources. The 2026/27 borrowing budget is £31.713m. Debt management budget shows £506k forecast underspend, suggesting possible timing benefits on interest costs depending on scheme delivery.
findings.matters: A £151m borrowing programme creates future revenue pressure through debt service; timing of drawdown against scheme delivery will affect in-year and forward interest cost forecasts at a time when service budgets are already under pressure.
findings.figures: Capital programme £371.8m (2026/27-2029/30 onwards), borrowing £151.4m (40%), external grants £195.9m (52%), 2026/27 borrowing budget £31.713m, debt management forecast underspend £506k
findings.quote: Borrowing represents 40% of funding with the remainder of the programme funded from revenue contribution and pooled resources (capital receipts generated by the sale of assets).

findings.paper_title: Item 8 First Quart Financial Outturn Position - Revenue and Capital Monitor Q1FINAL
findings.headline: Useable reserves forecast to decline 28.8% to £30.696m closing balance, with Schools/DSG reserves down 85%
findings.detail: Total opening balance £43.131m falls to forecast closing balance of £30.696m (-£12.435m, -28.8%). Decline includes £8.892m reduction in Schools and DSG reserves (£10.454m→£1.562m, -85%) as High Needs deficit accumulates. Forecast assumes year-end overspend will be recovered; if not, reserves would decline further.
findings.matters: A 28.8% reduction in reserves in a single year significantly constrains financial flexibility and reduces the buffer to manage unexpected demand changes or funding shortfalls, particularly acute as High Needs liabilities accumulate.
findings.figures: Opening useable reserves £43.131m, closing £30.696m (-£12.435m, -28.8%); General balances £7.689m→£8.369m, Schools/DSG £10.454m→£1.562m (-£8.892m, -85%)
findings.quote: The forecast closing position on reserves at 31 March 2027 is shown in the table below , this assumes that the forecast overspend will be recovered to a balanced position:

findings.paper_title: Item 8 First Quart Financial Outturn Position - Revenue and Capital Monitor Q1FINAL
findings.headline: High Needs deficit of £30.5m budgeted for 2026/27; Department for Education to cover 90%, residual 10% (£11m) to be charged to general fund from 2028/29
findings.detail: Costs of £69m against DSG funding of £38.5m create approved deficit covered under statutory override ending March 2028. Prior year recovery grant of £36.6m expected October 2026, but timing of Department for Education grants for 2026/27 and 2027/28 deficits not yet confirmed, creating uncertainty over when the £11m general fund liability will crystallize.
findings.matters: A crystallized future liability of £11m dependent on Department for Education funding creates uncertainty in general fund forecast and represents a material call on reserves after statutory override ends, occurring when overall reserves are already declining.
findings.figures: High Needs deficit £30.5m (costs £69m, funding £38.5m), opening balance £40.6m, forecast closing before grant £71.1m, DFE prior-year recovery grant £36.6m, residual 10% liability £11m from 2028/29
findings.quote: The DFE intends to fund 90% of the SEND deficit up to th e end of the statutory override period . The residual 10% will require funding from general balances and not Dedicated Schools Grant, this is estimated to be £11m in 2028/29 .

findings.paper_title: Item 8 First Quart Financial Outturn Position - Revenue and Capital Monitor Q1FINAL
findings.headline: Care home placements increased 34 people in six months; Mental Health placements up 31%, Learning Disabilities up 9%
findings.detail: Numbers in care homes grew from 664 to 698 between February and August 2026 (5.1% increase in six months), driven by 31% growth in Mental Health placements and 9% in Learning Disability placements. This sustained growth in both volume and complexity of need is the principal driver of the £4.586m Adult Social Care overspend.
findings.matters: Rapid growth in care home placements represents demand-led cost pressure that cannot be easily controlled without policy change or relocation of people, signaling a structural budget risk extending beyond the current year.
findings.figures: Care home numbers 664→698 (+34, +5.1% in six months); Mental Health placements +31%, Learning Disability placements +9%
findings.quote: Growth in care home numbers from 664 to 698 people between February and August 2026. Mental Health care home placements increasing by 31%. Learning Disability care home placements increasing by 9%.

findings.paper_title: Item 8 First Quart Financial Outturn Position - Revenue and Capital Monitor Q1FINAL
findings.headline: Adult Social Care savings only 11% delivered against £2.564m target
findings.detail: First quarter outturn shows only £291k (11%) of planned Adult and Wellbeing savings delivered. Remaining savings are contingent on completion of transformational work including deputyship and appointeeship fee charging, care charging policy, and financial assessment improvements. If not delivered, the £4.586m overspend will not be recovered through savings alone.
findings.matters: Undelivered savings in the overspending service area compound the budget pressure and indicate that planned transformation activities may not materialize, risking a widened deficit requiring council-wide solutions.
findings.figures: £291k delivered of £2.564m target (11%); Adult Social Care overspend £4.586m against budget of £101.57m
findings.quote: To date £ 291k or 11% have been delivered (across vacancy management and mental health provision review). Work is progressing on the charging policy for Deputyship and Appointeeship service fee .
